# About this script 

This script shows the workflow to evaluate spatial correlation in model residuals across the 1,000 phylogenetic scenarios. To do so we will use `spdep` and `SoDA` package, the latter was used to transform decimal degree coordinates into Cartesian. We followed the Appendix S2, sect. 4 of [Bauman et al., (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2469) to measure Moran's I and correct spatial autocorrelation (if needed).

**The output here is a supplement for Table 2 and Appendix S14 in the main text.**

![Note]: To hurry up the process we will use this function:

> ![WARNING] 
> Run this script demands a lot of memory and takes a minute to end. Therefore, clear garbage accumulated with `gc()`, the environment and restart the session. You may not be able to run this script if you have less than 8 GB of RAM.

# Packages, settings and functions

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

rm(list = ls())         # Clear all objects from the environment
gc()                    # Run garbage collection to free memory

# Function to compute MEM (Moran's Eigenvector Maps) and test for spatial autocorrelation
test_mem <- function(res, lw, nmodel = NULL) {
  mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = T)  # Run MEM selection with permutation

  # Extract global Moran’s I and p-value
  sac <- data.frame(
    I = mem$global.test$obs,
    Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
  ) %>%
    mutate(model = nmodel, .before = I) %>%
    `rownames<-`(NULL)

  # If MEM vectors were selected
  if (length(mem) > 1) {
    message('Check MEM data for eigenvectors...')
    mem_data <- list(
      sac = sac,                      # Moran's I summary
      selected.MEM = mem$MEM.select,  # Selected eigenvectors
      summary = mem$summary           # Full summary with p-values
    )
    return(mem_data)
  } else {
    message('No MEM selected...')
    return(sac)
  }
}

# Function to summarize model results: mean ± sd for each column (excluding model name)
get_df <- function (x) {
  model = x[1, 1]
  mean = t(apply(x[, -1], MARGIN = 2, function(y)
           {paste0(round(mean(y),3), '[±', round(sd (y),3), ']')}
           ))
  data.frame (model, mean)
}

# Packages
# devtools::install_github("cran/SoDA", force = T) #install SoDA to deal with coords
require(spdep)
library(ade4)
library(adespatial)
library(SoDA)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
library(sp)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

## Define reproducibility
set.seed(811)
## Set the return of numeric values only (not scientific notations)
options(scipen = 99997) 
# number of elements (ie. trees or repetitions)
N = 1000
```

# Load data

For this script we will need the CWM values computed before (`cwm_list.RDS`) alongside with environmental data, which we fortunately insert in the `cwm_values_raw.RDS`. 

```{r}

all_df <- readRDS(file = 'data/cwm_values_raw.RDS') %>%
  column_to_rownames('Site')  # Load original community-weighted mean values

models <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  "outputs/mod_select_cwm.xlsx",
  sheet = "nice_mode_S"
)  # Load selected models per trait

cwm_list <- readRDS("data/cwm_list.RDS")  # Load list of CWM matrices per trait and iteration
```

# Start parallel computing

```{r}
no_cores <- detectCores() - 6  # Use all cores minus 4 (adjust to 5 for desktop)
registerDoParallel(cores = no_cores)
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores, type = "FORK")  # Create parallel backend
```

# Spatial correlation
This procedure is very similar to that adopted in previous steps of this script list. The only difference, as before, it runs iteratively most steps, like the residuals extraction and Bauman et al., (2018) MEM selection. In summary we will:

1) Create a distance matrix with our coordinates;
2) Create a spatial weighted matrix (see Methods section);
3) Extract each models residuals (iteratively for the n-phylogenetic scenarios);
4) Run MEM selection with a custom function to hurry up the process;
5) Extract the needed information (Moran I, p-values, MEM selected and others minor things...).

## Creating coord. distance matrix

```{r}
## Creating a Cartesian coordinates df, which will permit Euclidean distance usage
df_xy <- SoDA::geoXY(
  latitude = all_df$Lat,
  longitude = all_df$Long,
  unit = 1000
)
dist <- dist(df_xy) # Compute Euclidean distances
```

# Spatial Weighted Matrix

```{r}
nb <- chooseCN(coordinates(df_xy), type = 4, plot.nb = FALSE)  # Create neighborhood graph (MST)
distnb <- nbdists(nb, df_xy)  # Get pairwise distances for each link
fdist <- lapply(distnb, function(x) 1 - x / max(dist(df_xy)))  # Convert distances to similarity weights

# Create listw object (spatial weights)
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = 'B', glist = fdist, zero.policy = TRUE)
```

# Creating a connectivity matrix based in Bauman (2018) proceed

```{r}
models$models
# Rhizome diameter
models[grep("Diam", models$models), ]$models
model <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  # Create model iteratively for the 1000 phylo scenarios
  lm(
    cwm_list$diam[[i]] ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
    data = all_df
  )

# Extract residual
res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

# Mesure Moran I and p-values
mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Rhizome diam. ~N')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

# Get summary model results
sac_diam <- get_df(mem)

# Compact Rhizome
models$models
model <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(cwm_list$r_comp[[i]] ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size, data = all_df)

mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Rhiz. Comp~N')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

sac_rcomp <- get_df(mem)

# Short Creeping Rhizome
models$models
model <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(cwm_list$r_cr[[i]] ~ ann_prec + prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size, data = all_df)

res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Rhiz. Short~AP+PS')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

sac_rcr <- get_df(mem)

# Multipinnate laminae
models$models
model <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(cwm_list$l_mseg[[i]] ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size, data = all_df)

res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Multipinnate~AP')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

sac_lmseg <- get_df(mem)

# Buds
models[grep("buds", models$models), ]$models

model <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(cwm_list$buds[[i]] ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size, data = all_df)

res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Buds~AP')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

sac_buds <- get_df(mem)

# Spore Chlorophyll
models[grep("Chl", models$models), ]$models

model <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(cwm_list$chl[[i]] ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size, data = all_df)

res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

mem <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    test_mem(res[[i]], lw, nmodel = 'Chlorophyll ~ PS')
  } %>%
  list_rbind()

sac_chl <- get_df(mem)
```

# Saving data

This data will supplement the Table 2 and Appendix S14.

```{r}
# Combine all in a matrix
cor_df <-
  rbind(sac_diam, sac_rcr, sac_rcomp, sac_lmseg, sac_buds,  sac_chl)


cor_df$data <- paste0(cor_df$I,"(", cor_df$Pvalue,")") 

cor_df

#Save data
wb_s_correl <-openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  file = "outputs/models_sac_scomp.xlsx",
  x = list(df = cor_df)
)
```
